description: An introduction to biology and its branches, the characteristics that distinguish living from non-living things, and the importance and applications of biology in everyday life.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of the word "Biology"?
mcq.explanation: "Biology" comes from Greek bios (life) and logos (study). Combined they mean the study of life. Biology is the study of living things (organisms). Exam Tip: A and C are branches of biology (botany and zoology), not biology itself. When a definition option is narrower than the whole subject, it is a distractor.

mcq.questionText: The branch of biology that deals with the study of plants is called:
mcq.explanation: The key word is "plants". Botany is the study of plant life. Exam Tip: Pair the roots: Botany-plants, Zoology-animals, Microbiology-microorganisms.

mcq.questionText: The branch of biology that deals with the study of animals is:
mcq.explanation: The key word is "animals". Zoo- refers to animals, so the study of animals is Zoology. Exam Tip: The "zoo" prefix is the memory hook - a zoo holds animals.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of living things?
mcq.explanation: The true characteristics of life are nutrition, respiration, movement, growth, reproduction, excretion and sensitivity. Rusting is a chemical reaction of iron, not a life process. Exam Tip: The mnemonic MR NIGER D (Movement, Respiration, Nutrition, Irritability, Growth, Excretion, Reproduction, Death) lists all life processes - anything outside it is a distractor.

mcq.questionText: The study of the relationship between living organisms and their environment is called:
mcq.explanation: The key phrase is "organisms and their environment". Eco- refers to environment, so this is Ecology. Exam Tip: "Eco" always signals environment. Don't confuse with Genetics (inheritance) or Physiology (functioning).

mcq.questionText: The process by which living things release energy from food is called:
mcq.explanation: The key phrase is "release energy from food". Respiration breaks down glucose inside cells to release energy. Exam Tip: Nutrition = obtaining food; Respiration = releasing energy from it.

mcq.questionText: The removal of metabolic waste products from the body of an organism is called:
mcq.explanation: The key phrase is "metabolic waste products". Excretion removes wastes made by body reactions, such as carbon dioxide and urea. Exam Tip: Excretion (metabolic waste, e.g. urea) differs from egestion (undigested food, i.e. faeces).

mcq.questionText: The ability of living organisms to respond to changes in their environment is called:
mcq.explanation: The key phrase is "respond to changes". Sensitivity (irritability) is detecting and responding to stimuli. Exam Tip: Sensitivity = irritability - both accepted. Example: a plant shoot bending towards light.

mcq.questionText: The branch of biology which deals with the study of cells is called:
mcq.explanation: The key word is "cells". Cyto- means cell, so the study of cells is Cytology. Exam Tip: Cyto = cell. Histology is the study of tissues - one level up from cells.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument is used to observe very small organisms that cannot be seen with the naked eye?
mcq.explanation: A microscope magnifies tiny specimens greatly, hundreds to thousands of times. Exam Tip: A hand lens magnifies only about x10; a microscope is needed for cells and microorganisms. A telescope is for distant, large objects.

mcq.questionText: Movement of the whole body of an organism from one place to another is called:
mcq.explanation: The key phrase is "whole body from one place to another". Locomotion is whole-body movement such as walking, swimming or flying. Exam Tip: Movement can be of a part; locomotion is the whole organism relocating. Plants show movement but not locomotion.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following shows that a motor car is NOT a living thing, even though it moves and uses fuel?
mcq.explanation: A car moves, uses fuel and releases exhaust gases, but cannot reproduce, grow, respond to stimuli or feed itself. The inability to reproduce shows it is non-living. Exam Tip: The giveaways of non-living things are no reproduction, no growth, no sensitivity.

mcq.questionText: The study of the internal structure of organisms is called:
mcq.explanation: The key word is "internal structure". Anatomy examines internal structures such as organs and tissues. Exam Tip: Anatomy = internal structure; Morphology = external structure (shape and form).

mcq.questionText: Which one of the following is a reason for studying biology?

options.text: To learn how to drive vehicles
To understand ourselves and other living things

mcq.explanation: Biology helps us understand our bodies, health, other organisms and the environment. Exam Tip: Distractors belong to engineering or ICT. Biology links to health, agriculture, medicine, nutrition and environment.

mcq.questionText: Living things increase permanently in size and mass through the process of:
mcq.explanation: The key phrase is "increase permanently in size and mass". Growth is the permanent, irreversible increase in size and mass. Exam Tip: The word "permanent" rules out temporary swelling. Growth results from cell division and enlargement.

fib.questionText: The word biology is derived from two Greek words, bios meaning ____ and logos meaning study.
fib.explanation: Bios means life and logos means study, so biology is the study of life. Exam Tip: This word-origin question appears almost every year - memorise both roots.

fib.questionText: The branch of biology that deals with the study of microorganisms is called ____.
fib.explanation: Micro- means very small, so microbiology is the study of microorganisms. Exam Tip: Microorganisms include bacteria, viruses, some fungi and protoctists.

fib.questionText: The characteristic of living things by which they produce new individuals of their own kind is called ____.
fib.explanation: Producing new individuals of the same kind is reproduction. Exam Tip: Reproduction replaces organisms lost by death; without it a species becomes extinct.

fib.questionText: The scientist who studies the classification of living organisms is called a ____.
fib.explanation: Classification of organisms is taxonomy, and the scientist who does it is a taxonomist. Exam Tip: Match the "-ist": taxonomy to taxonomist, ecology to ecologist, botany to botanist.

fib.questionText: The study of the functioning or working of the body of organisms is called ____.
fib.explanation: Physiology deals with how the body and its parts work. Exam Tip: Anatomy asks "what is the structure?"; Physiology asks "how does it work?".

fib.questionText: Organisms made up of only one cell are called ____ organisms.
fib.explanation: Uni- means one, so an organism of a single cell is unicellular. Exam Tip: Examples: amoeba, euglena, paramecium, yeast, bacteria. Opposite is multicellular.

fib.questionText: The characteristic of living things that involves taking in and using food is called ____.
fib.explanation: Taking in and using food is nutrition. Exam Tip: Plants make their own food (autotrophic); animals feed on ready-made food (heterotrophic).

fib.questionText: The study of insects is a branch of biology called ____.
fib.explanation: Entomology is the specific branch dealing with insects. Exam Tip: Entomology (insects), Ichthyology (fish), Virology (viruses), Bacteriology (bacteria).

fib.questionText: Biology is applied in the field of ____ to improve crop and animal production.
fib.explanation: Improving crops and animals is farming, which is agriculture. Exam Tip: Know at least four applied fields - agriculture, medicine, nutrition, veterinary/pharmacy.

fib.questionText: The gradual change of an organism over a long period of time to suit its environment is studied under the concept of ____.
fib.explanation: Gradual change over a long time across generations is evolution. Exam Tip: Evolution is long-term change across generations; adaptation is the feature that results.

tf.questionText: All living things are made up of cells.
tf.explanation: Every living organism is built from one or more cells. Exam Tip: This is the cell theory in one sentence.

tf.questionText: Plants are able to move their whole body from one place to another.
tf.explanation: Plants can move parts such as leaves and roots but cannot relocate their whole body, so they lack locomotion. Exam Tip: Plants show movement of parts but not locomotion.

tf.questionText: Respiration and breathing mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: Breathing supplies oxygen to the body, while respiration uses that oxygen to release energy from food inside cells. Exam Tip: Breathing supplies oxygen; respiration uses it to release energy.

tf.questionText: Zoology is the branch of biology that deals with the study of animals.
tf.explanation: Zoo- refers to animals, so zoology is correctly the study of animals. Exam Tip: Zoo- refers to animals.

tf.questionText: A motor car is considered a living thing because it moves and uses fuel.
tf.explanation: A car imitates only a few processes but cannot reproduce, grow or respond, and life requires all characteristics together. Exam Tip: Life requires ALL characteristics together; a car imitates only two or three.

tf.questionText: The study of biology is important in the field of medicine.
tf.explanation: Biology underpins medicine by explaining the body, diseases and treatments. Exam Tip: Medicine, agriculture, nutrition and conservation are standard "importance of biology" answers.

tf.questionText: Excretion is the removal of undigested food materials from the body.
tf.explanation: Excretion removes metabolic waste such as urea, whereas the removal of undigested food is egestion. Exam Tip: Excretion removes metabolic waste; removal of undigested food is egestion.

tf.questionText: Unicellular organisms are made up of many cells.
tf.explanation: Uni- means one, so unicellular organisms have only a single cell, not many. Exam Tip: Uni = 1, multi = many. The statement contradicts its own prefix.

tf.questionText: Sensitivity enables organisms to detect and respond to changes in their surroundings.
tf.explanation: Sensitivity is exactly the ability to detect stimuli and respond to changes in the environment. Exam Tip: Sensitivity helps organisms find food, avoid danger and adapt.

tf.questionText: Growth in living organisms is a temporary increase in size that can be reversed.
tf.explanation: Growth is a permanent, irreversible increase in size and mass, not a temporary reversible change. Exam Tip: Growth is a permanent increase; temporary swelling from water is not growth.

summary.correctAnswer: The scientific study of living things (organisms), from the Greek bios meaning life and logos meaning study.
summary.explanation: Biology covers all life, from tiny microorganisms to plants and animals. Exam Tip: Remember the two Greek roots bios and logos.

summary.correctAnswer: The branch of biology that deals with the study of plants.
summary.explanation: Botany covers plant structure, function, growth and classification. Exam Tip: Pair Botany with plants and Zoology with animals.

summary.correctAnswer: The branch of biology that deals with the study of animals.
summary.explanation: The zoo- prefix links directly to animals. Exam Tip: A zoo holds animals is the memory hook.

summary.correctAnswer: The study of the relationship between living organisms and their environment.
summary.explanation: Eco- always signals the environment and the interactions within it. Exam Tip: Do not confuse Ecology with Genetics or Physiology.

summary.questionText: Characteristics of living things (MR NIGER D)
summary.correctAnswer: Movement, Respiration, Nutrition, Irritability, Growth, Excretion, Reproduction and Death - the life processes shown by all living things.
summary.explanation: A true living thing must show all of these characteristics together. Exam Tip: Anything outside MR NIGER D is a distractor in the exam.

summary.correctAnswer: The process by which living things release energy from food by breaking down glucose inside cells.
summary.explanation: Respiration provides the energy needed for all other life processes. Exam Tip: Do not confuse respiration with breathing or with nutrition.

summary.correctAnswer: Excretion is the removal of metabolic waste such as carbon dioxide and urea, while egestion is the removal of undigested food (faeces).
summary.explanation: The two are commonly confused but describe different wastes. Exam Tip: Metabolic waste means excretion; undigested food means egestion.

summary.correctAnswer: The basic structural and functional unit of all living things.
summary.explanation: All organisms are made of one or more cells, as stated by the cell theory. Exam Tip: Cytology is the branch of biology that studies cells.

summary.correctAnswer: An organism made up of only one cell, such as amoeba, paramecium, yeast or bacteria.
summary.explanation: Uni- means one, the opposite of a multicellular organism which has many cells. Exam Tip: Learn examples like amoeba and euglena.

summary.correctAnswer: Biology helps us understand ourselves and other living things and is applied in fields such as medicine, agriculture and nutrition.
summary.explanation: Its applications improve health, food production and care of the environment. Exam Tip: Know at least four applied fields for the exam.

hoq.questionText: A student observed an object that moves, takes in materials and releases gases, but over several weeks it neither grew larger nor produced any offspring. Using biological characteristics, the object is best described as:

options.text: A living thing because it moves and releases gases
A non-living thing because it lacks growth and reproduction
A plant because it releases gases
A microorganism because it takes in materials

hoq.explanation: The object shows movement, gaseous exchange and intake, but lacks growth and reproduction. A true living thing must show all characteristics of life, so missing growth and reproduction means it is non-living. Exam Tip: A is the trap - it judges life from two processes only. Absence of growth and reproduction is decisive.

hoq.questionText: A researcher works on developing better crop varieties, treating plant diseases and improving soil fertility. Which combination of biology branches and applied fields is she MOST directly using?
hoq.explanation: "Crop varieties" and "plant diseases" concern plants, which is Botany, while "soil fertility" and "crop production" concern farming, which is Agriculture. Botany and agriculture fit both halves. Exam Tip: Application questions reward reading BOTH clues (plants + farming). A single-clue match is usually a distractor.

hoq.questionText: A form one student argues that a candle flame is alive because it moves (flickers), feeds (on wax), respires (uses air), grows (gets taller) and excretes (produces smoke). Which characteristic of living things does the flame TRULY lack, proving it is non-living?
hoq.explanation: The flame's flicker, wax-consuming, air use, rising and smoke are pseudo-processes. A flame cannot produce new flames by a life process nor detect and respond to stimuli in a controlled way, so it genuinely lacks reproduction and sensitivity. Exam Tip: A flame splitting is not biological reproduction, and its response is purely physical. Always ask: does it REPRODUCE and truly RESPOND?
